newsitem.title: MEXICO: Penoles numbers seen stagnant to yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Penoles numbers seen stagnant to yr-end.

text.p: Doldrums for Mexican mining giant Penoles should turn by the end of the year or in 1998, analysts said.
"Investors should bite the bullet and write off earnings in 1997. We're looking at a stable year, about a five percent decline in earnings," Merrill Lynch's Rene Kleyweg said.
Analysts said the world's largest silver producer dug up more of the same in the second quarter.
Battered by a strong peso and depressed precious metal prices, the company reported earnings per share for the second quarter of 0.69 peso, compared to an Reuters forecast of 0.71 from four analysts.
Net profits for the first half were 567.06 million from 575.48 million in 1996.
"I think they're doing everything they can to keep margins up and costs down, same old story," Paribas Nigel Kieser in London said.

But higher sales volumes were not enough to combat the lower international gold and silver prices and the peso's appreciation. A more expensive peso hurts the company's largely dollar-denominated sales.

Penoles' revenues for the first half of the year were 3.411 billion pesos, down from 3.757 billion pesos in the year-ago period. Operating profits for the first six months were 701.26 million pesos, compared with 1.013 billion pesos in 1996.
"The results were in line with what I was estimating ... given the environment they faced with weak metal prices and a strong peso," Santander's Sandra Morfin in Mexico City said.
But Kleyweg said operations were also weak in the quarter.
"The weakness comes from the operating side," the New York analyst said. "The fact is we saw a bigger impact from (the cost of) maintenance operations."
Even weaker gold prices expected in the third quarter could point to another lukewarm report then, analysts said.

But by the end of the year or early 1998, they said the company should begin to reap the benefits of greater own-mined production from projects in the works. Analysts also expected gold and silver prices to bounce from low levels.
Penoles has alloted $644 million in investments through 1999, and has earmarked $365 million to shop for possible joint ventures or new acquisitions.
Analysts have said benefits from these investments will start to be seen in improved operating margins by 1998, as the company boost its own-mined output from new mines.

The company's La Herradura 150,000 ounce per year gold mine is due for start-up in the second quarter of 1998. The Mezcala 150,000 ounce per year gold mine and Francisco Madero 96,000 ounce zinc mine will follow in 1999.

Penoles also said in a statement it expects to spend about $80 million on the Pinos Altos 100,000-120,000 ounce gold project. An additional $100 million is slated for an unspecified energy cogeneration project that aims to cut energy costs by 25 percent.
